Loan agreement LOA-6571 shows a £15,450 loan to the customer for a used car, and dealer invoice INV-3120 bills the customer exactly £17,200 for a 2020 hatchback (LP21 JXX), with the balance from own funds.

why_not.ESCALATE: A documented car purchase funded by a loan isn't a pass-through.
why_not.RFI: The loan agreement and invoice already document the flow.

doubts: A 2020 model on a 21 plate (registered March-August 2021) is possible if first registered later, but slightly unusual.

sop_basis: TM02; TM04 more than 6 counterparties; collection without documents
rationale: Between 30 Jul and 8 Aug 2026 Kai Bramden received 13 payments of £185.00, mostly referencing a Snowdonia trip, and paid £2,590.00 to Caldale Travel Ltd, ref 'BOOKING GT32964' (14 x £185). The pattern fits a group trip collection, but no booking confirmation is on file to tie the payers to the booking. Request it.

why_not.CLOSE: No booking confirmation documents the collection or the payers.
why_not.ESCALATE: Small equal contributions paid on to a travel company look legitimate.

sop_basis: TM07 dormant reactivation; returning-customer close needs evidence
rationale: After 279 days dormant, Peyton Draycote received £8,775.00 by SWIFT from an own-name account in the UAE, ref 'SAVINGS', 4.5 times monthly income, followed only by a small card payment. There's no overseas account statement and no reverification to confirm current circumstances. Ask for both.

why_not.CLOSE: With no statement or reverification, a returning-customer close isn't supported.
why_not.ESCALATE: An own-name transfer with only ordinary spending afterwards isn't suspicious.

sop_basis: TM01 income multiple; documented one-off event
rationale: Rowan Bromhurst received £48,169.48 from Drayridge Solicitors LLP's client account on 13 Oct 2026, ref 'ESTATE OF TAYLOR CRANDEN'. Solicitor letter SOL-2919 (9 Oct 2026) confirms the firm acts for the executors of Taylor Cranden's estate and that the recipient's entitlement is exactly £48,169.48, to be paid that week. The funds remain in the account.

why_not.ESCALATE: A documented inheritance from a solicitor's client account isn't suspicious.
why_not.RFI: The solicitor's letter documents the source and amount.

doubts: The letter has no addressee or salutation naming the customer, but it ties to the estate, amount, firm and timing.

sop_basis: TM02; TM04 more than 6 counterparties; documented group collection
rationale: Between 12 and 21 Sep 2026 Max Glencote received 11 payments of £260.00 referencing an Edinburgh trip and paid £3,120.00 to Radton Travel Ltd, ref 'BOOKING BK46821'. Booking confirmation BKG-7053 names the customer as lead traveller for 12 people at £260 each (£3,120 total, due 21 Sep). All 11 payers appear on its traveller list.

why_not.ESCALATE: Small equal contributions from named travellers paid on to a travel company are not suspicious.
why_not.RFI: The booking documents the collection and every payer.

sop_basis: TM01 income multiple; own-account transfer large relative to profile
rationale: Jules Marmore received £16,760.60 'OWN ACCOUNT' on 19 Aug 2026 from their own Kestrel Mutual account, which statement STM-4360 confirms. Own funds explain the source, but the amount is about 5.5 times declared monthly income. Ask the customer to update their profile and the purpose of the move.

why_not.CLOSE: Ownership is shown, but a transfer this large against the profile warrants a profile refresh.
why_not.ESCALATE: A documented transfer between the customer's own accounts isn't suspicious.

doubts: This is a toss-up with CLOSE OWN_ACCOUNT, since ownership is documented and the multiple is borderline.

sop_basis: TM01; TM02; TM05; inconsistent explanations, funds moved abroad
rationale: Teddy Talcombe, a student on a £650 allowance, deposited £20,700 cash on 15-16 Aug 2026 and on 16 Aug sent £20,100 by SWIFT to Marley Wenton in Spain as 'family support' for a family friend. They told staff the cash was a gift from an uncle (CHT-641), then said the next day it came from selling their car (CHT-7145), with no documents for either.

why_not.CLOSE: The source of funds is contradictory and undocumented.
why_not.RFI: Conflicting explanations, then near-total movement abroad within a day, warrant escalation.

doubts: Spain isn't a higher-risk country; the escalation rests on the contradictory source of funds and the immediate pass-through.

sop_basis: TM05 cash £10,000+; TM01; documented one-off event
rationale: Robin Bromden deposited £15,450.00 cash on 16 Oct 2026. Private sale receipt SAL-9223 (15 Oct 2026), signed by both parties, records the sale of a 2021 hatchback RQ21 UPX (52,000 miles) to Frankie Calbrook for exactly £15,450.00 cash. Insurance schedule INS-9881 shows the customer insured that vehicle, confirming ownership. The 21 plate matches the 2021 model year.

why_not.ESCALATE: A documented one-off car sale isn't suspicious.
why_not.RFI: The sale receipt and insurance schedule already document the source.

sop_basis: TM01; TM02; TM04; money mule indicators with fraud reports
rationale: Hayden Kelby, a 19-year-old warehouse operative, received £12,100 from 10 unrelated people (9-13 Aug 2026) with mixed references and moved 92% out within 48 hours through repeated Coinvale Exchange crypto payments and ATM withdrawals. In CHT-1596 they describe a social-media 'payments assistant' job: clients pay in, they forward to the company's crypto account and keep 8%, with no contract and no one met. Two sending banks have reported APP scams (RPT-6844, RPT-9323) for incoming payments.

why_not.CLOSE: The flows are classic mule activity with fraud reports.
why_not.RFI: The customer's own account and two APP fraud reports already establish mule activity; escalation is required.

doubts: The customer is likely a recruited, possibly unwitting, mule.

sop_basis: TM03 cash deposits of £9,000-£9,999.99; business records reconcile
rationale: Wilwick Parking Ltd made four cash deposits of £9,060-£9,915 between 7 and 15 Sep 2026, each referencing a car park's takings. Collection reports COL-8218 match every amount, with safe bag numbers, and each deposit falls the morning after the emptying date set in procedure PRC-2577 (Ashbrook Street on Sundays, Glenbrook Road on Mondays). The pattern was reviewed and closed in June 2026 (BK-R926905), and turnover of £1.535m supports these takings.

why_not.ESCALATE: Sub-£10k deposits come from documented separate weekly site takings, not structuring.
why_not.RFI: The business records already reconcile every deposit.

sop_basis: TM07 dormant reactivation; returning customer with own-name funds verified
rationale: After 235 days dormant, Sidney Wilbrook received £7,922.79 by SWIFT from their own account at Everholt Bank PJSC in the UAE, ref 'SAVINGS', followed by a small card payment. Statement STM-1301 confirms the account is in the customer's name and shows the transfer. Reverification RVF-9602 (3 Sep 2026) confirmed identity on the registered device and the address, and the customer said they had been working in Dubai.

why_not.ESCALATE: A returning customer bringing home their own overseas savings isn't suspicious.
why_not.RFI: Ownership of the source account and the customer's identity are already verified.

doubts: The customer says they've been in Dubai 'for the past year', but UK rent and bills ran until January 2026. That's minor, as standing orders can run while abroad.

sop_basis: TM01; plausible one-off event with no documents
rationale: Jules Norholt received £44,308.31 from Selstead Solicitors LLP's client account on 14 Aug 2026, ref 'ESTATE OF AVERY WENGATE', about 16 times monthly income. An inheritance is plausible, but no solicitor or executor letter is on file. Request the solicitor's letter confirming the entitlement.

why_not.CLOSE: The inheritance is undocumented.
why_not.ESCALATE: Funds from a solicitor's client account referencing an estate, with no onward movement, are not suspicious.
